svg.title: Figure 2 — Swin-Tiny phase classifier with dihedral TTA
svg.text: Figure 2 | Stage-4 phase classifier: Swin-Tiny with 8-fold dihedral test-time augmentation
One segmented crop per frame → 8 symmetry-equivalent views → shared Swin-Tiny → averaged posterior → per-frame phase label
p̄ = ⅛ Σ softmax( f(g·x) ), g ∈ D₄
two residual sub-blocks: windowed self-attention, then a 4× MLP.
The pair is the unit — attention only crosses windows via the shift.
consecutive blocks alternate the two, so information crosses window
boundaries. Long-range structure — a five-fold twin spanning the whole
particle — becomes visible while attention stays local and cheap.
the crystallographic phase is invariant under rotation and reflection
— a decahedron turned 90° is still a decahedron. These are therefore 8
genuinely equivalent observations of one label, and averaging them
Ih and Ih→Dh are not separable from a single frame — a 4-class model
reaches only 89.3 %. They are merged here, and the transition is
recovered from temporal context (Fig. 1, Temporal Smoothing Head).
real particle-level split — 1 214 of 12 116 images, split 90/10 by particle
Ensembling was tested and rejected — the weaker members drag the mean below the single best model with TTA.
cross-entropy, label smoothing 0.05, inverse-frequency class weights
WeightedRandomSampler power 1.0 — classes fully equalised per epoch
AdamW, lr 1e-4 (warm-start) / 3e-4, weight decay 1e-4, cosine annealing
batch 32, 20–25 epochs, seed 44, best-val checkpoint kept
jitter 0.2 — exact rotations only, because interpolation destroys the
lattice fringes the model classifies on
backbone from a prior 3-class checkpoint; without it training collapses
by PARTICLE, not by image — both frames of a particle stay on one side
